`benmore create-app <name> [--json]` creates a deployed app (the `create_app` tool). `--json` prints the tool's JSON answer unchanged; without it the CLI prints the new subdomain and URL as text. Run in a folder that holds app.yaml or schema.prisma and no .benmore/app marker, it creates the app without the starter's demo files and links the folder to it, so the next `benmore deploy` ships the local files.
`benmore delete <app> --confirm` removes the app (api(at:"recovery") delete_app). `-y` is accepted in place of `--confirm`; without either the command refuses (exit 1) and sends nothing.

`benmore billing [--json]` prints the signed-in account's plan and what it uses of it, one line each: the account's email, the plan, published (live) apps used of allowed, apps in total used of allowed, collaborator seats used of allowed (only when the plan has seats or some are in use), the database storage limit per app in human units and bytes, and hosted media storage used of the allowance. A limit the plan does not have reads `(no limit)`; extra live-app slots and seats the account bought are named on their line. `--json` prints the platform's answer unchanged (GET /platform/billing/me): `plan`, `live_apps_used`, `live_app_limit`, `app_count`, `total_app_limit`, `seats_used`, `seat_limit`, `storage_per_app_mb`, `media_bytes_used`, `media_bytes_limit` and the rest of that answer, with a limit null when unlimited. It reads only: it takes no argument and no `--env`, it answers for the account the token belongs to and cannot name another, and it changes no plan or add-on (the account holder does that on the dashboard's /upgrade page). A rejected token exits 4. The numbers are the ones the publish gate and collaborator invites check (api(at:"environments") `publishing`, api(at:"collaborators") `plans`). `storage_per_app_mb` is the plan's limit; one app's own database size and limit: `benmore health <app>` (api(at:"errors") `cli`).
`benmore sync [--force]` pulls every app in the account's app list into the Benmore workspace (api(at:"sync-status") workspace_sync).

`benmore tool <name> [key=val ...] [--args-json '<json>'] [--env dev|prod]` calls any platform MCP tool by name and prints its text answer; an image in the answer (a browser_check screenshot) is saved to a temporary file whose path is printed. `true`, `false`, `null`, whole numbers and values that parse as a JSON array or object are sent typed, everything else as a string; `--args-json` supplies the arguments as one JSON object. `--env` (else the `benmore use` pin) is sent as the tool's `env` argument unless an `env=` argument names one. A tool error prints the tool's message on stderr and exits 1.
